title: J-2 can be tested on module-finite algebras
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose that for every commutative $R$-algebra $B$ which is finitely generated as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], the subset $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B:B_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is Zariski open [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then for every finite type commutative $R$-algebra $C$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], the subset $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}C:C_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is Zariski open. Equivalently, $R$ is J-2 in the sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (3) implies (1); J-1 and J-2 expanded by Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and a finite purely inseparable extension $L/k$, where $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Put $A=R/\mathfrak p$, viewed inside $k$ and then $L$. The fraction description in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] identifies $k$ with the fractions of $A$: send $r/s$ modulo $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ to $(r+\mathfrak p)/(s+\mathfrak p)$. The denominators are nonzero because $s\notin\mathfrak p$; both equality relations are $rs'-r's\in\mathfrak p$, since primality cancels any additional multiplier outside $\mathfrak p$. Thus this map is a well-defined bijection respecting addition and multiplication, and $A$ is a domain embedded in $L$.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (3) implies (4), followed by (4) implies (1); Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: In characteristic zero [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] says $L=k$; take $B=A$, generated as an $R$-module by $1$, and skip to step 4. In positive characteristic $p$, choose a finite $k$-basis $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_t$ of $L$. For each $i$, pure inseparability gives $n_i=p^{e_i}\geq1$ and $\alpha_i^{n_i}=c_i/d_i$ with $c_i,d_i\in A$ and $d_i\ne0$. Set $\beta_i=d_i\alpha_i\in L$. Then $\beta_i^{n_i}=c_i d_i^{n_i-1}\in A$. This explicit identity, including the case $n_i=1$, supplies a monic power relation with coefficients in $A$ for each scaled basis element.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (3) implies (4), followed by (4) implies (1); Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: In positive characteristic define $B=A[\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_t]\subseteq L$. Repeatedly replace $\beta_i^{n_i}$ by $c_i d_i^{n_i-1}$ in a polynomial: the finitely many monomials $\beta_1^{j_1}\cdots\beta_t^{j_t}$ with $0\leq j_i<n_i$ span $B$ over $A$. As $R\to A$ is surjective, they also span $B$ over $R$, exactly the finiteness of [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The fractions of $B$ exhaust $L$: they contain the fractions $k$ of $A$ and each $\alpha_i=\beta_i/d_i$, so they contain every $k$-linear combination of the basis. Conversely every such fraction belongs to the field $L$. In either characteristic $B$ is a domain, since it is a subring of $L$.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (3) implies (4), followed by (4) implies (1); Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: The ring $B$ is a commutative $R$-algebra finite as an $R$-module, in either case above. Since $R$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. The hypothesis of the item applied to this particular $B$ now says that $U=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B:B_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (3) implies (4), followed by (4) implies (1); Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: This open $U$ is nonempty: the zero ideal is prime in the nonzero domain $B$, and its localization consists of all fractions of $B$, hence is $L$. A field has just the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, is Noetherian and local with zero maximal ideal, and has Krull dimension zero. Its maximal ideal is generated by the empty list. Thus it is regular local by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The zero prime therefore belongs to $U$. This proves the nonempty regular-open condition, without any reducedness assumption on $R$.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (3) implies (4), followed by (4) implies (1); Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: For every $\mathfrak p$ and every finite purely inseparable extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ we have constructed an $R$-subalgebra $B\subseteq L$, finite as an $R$-module, with all fractions equal to $L$, and with a nonempty regular open. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-exc-j2-residue-field-criterion], whose statement gives openness of the regular locus for every finite type $R$-algebra. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] this is precisely the J-2 condition, proving both formulations of the conclusion. If $R$ is the zero ring, the residue-field condition has no instances and the same criterion applies.
